title: The Night Something Walked Across England

basis.note: not enough measured videos yet; using fixed default

segments.narration: On February 8, 1855, the townspeople of Devon woke to a nightmare in the fresh snow.
Cloven hoofprints stretched across forty miles. Not side by side—a single line, perfectly straight.
They marched over fourteen-foot stone walls, across freezing rivers, and onto high rooftops. What kind of creature ignores physics?
Panicked villagers followed the trail to locked barns and narrow drainpipes. The footprints passed straight through solid wood.
The snow eventually melted, but the terror stayed. Deep inside every print, the frozen earth was scorched black.

verdicts.claim: On February 8, 1855, mysterious footprints appeared in snow across Devon, England.
verdicts.note: The article states that on the night of 8–9 February 1855, mysterious hoof-like marks appeared in the snow across Devon, England.

verdicts.claim: The prints resembled cloven hooves and formed a single straight line.
verdicts.note: The article notes that comparisons were made to cloven hooves and that the footprints appeared mostly in a single file, traveling straight over obstacles.

verdicts.claim: The trail stretched for dozens of miles across more than thirty locations.
verdicts.note: The article confirms the total distance of the tracks was estimated between 40 and 100 miles, reported from more than 30 locations.

verdicts.claim: The footprints appeared on top of high walls, snow-covered roofs, and locked enclosures.
verdicts.note: The article mentions prints appearing on snow-covered roofs, high walls, and yards/gardens enclosed by high walls and palings.
